featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Chili’s Grill & Bar in Powai, and overall, it was a solid 4-star experience. Chili’s has always been known for its dependable food quality, and that part still remains intact. We ordered the Chicken Platter, which comes with a nice customisation option. The portion size was good, the flavours were balanced, and everything was served hot and well-prepared. It’s the kind of comfort food Chili’s is known for, and it didn’t disappoint.

For drinks, I tried their Mango Mocktail, and it was easily one of the highlights of the evening. Refreshing, smooth, and perfectly sweet — I liked it so much that I ended up ordering it twice. Their beer selection was also good, maintaining the familiar Chili’s standard.

However, a few things held the experience back from being a full 5-star visit. The first noticeable issue was the pre-added 10% tip on the bill. While I fully support tipping for good service, adding it automatically and at a relatively high percentage didn’t feel right — especially considering the level of service we received. The service wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t exceptional enough to justify a mandatory 10% charge. Tips should always feel voluntary and earned, not forced.

The ambience also felt different compared to the older Chili’s outlets. One thing that always made Chili’s special was its distinct American pub-style vibe — warm lighting, rustic interiors, and a lively but cozy atmosphere. The Powai outlet, unfortunately, doesn’t quite capture that same charm. The décor and layout feel more like a typical modern Indian pub, lacking the signature Chili’s personality that many of us associate with the brand. It’s decent, but it doesn’t stand out the way earlier Chili’s interiors used to.

That said, the environment is still comfortable for dining, and the place is clean, spacious, and well-maintained. The overall quality of food and drinks remains trustworthy, and if you’re looking for a casual evening out with good food, Chili’s Powai is still a reliable choice.

In summary, the experience was enjoyable — great food, excellent mocktails, and a relaxed vibe — but with room for improvement in service transparency and ambience. A good outing overall, deserving of four stars.

We went to Mainland China on Monday to try some nice authentic Chinese food. Surprisingly, they had a Six Course Set Menu starting at ₹795 for veg and ₹895 for non-veg and honestly, it’s worth every penny.

We both tried the veg and non-veg options and loved everything from start to finish. The food was absolutely delicious and tasted genuinely authentic. Even the Cantonese Clear Soup, at first, looks like just plain water, but once you taste it, you won’t stop. The flavor is so comforting and light, yet rich in taste.

For dumplings, we had Truffle Oil Infused Edamame, Corn and Water Chestnut, Sriracha Chicken, and Chicken Siu Mai. All were perfectly steamed and flavorful.

In starters, we tried Turnip Cake Salt and Pepper, Jiang’s Chilli Cottage Cheese, Chicken with Assorted Pepper, and Sliced Chicken in Chilli Oil with Spring Onion. Every dish was cooked to perfection.

For the main course, we went with Stir Fried Chinese Greens, Vegetables in Yellow Bean Sauce, Fish in Roasted Garlic Sauce, and Stir Fried Chicken in Mountain Chilli Sauce. These were paired beautifully with Korean Sweet Potato Noodles, Wok Tossed Hakka Noodles, and Edamame Jasmine Fried Rice.

The dessert, Honey Noodles with Almond Flakes served with a Chocolate Cigar Roll, was the highlight of the meal. It’s crunchy, chocolaty, and so addictive that you’ll want another serving.

We also tried their mocktails, which were quite refreshing and paired well with the food.

Overall, the experience was amazing from the service to the presentation. At this price, the Six Course Lunch Menu is totally worth it. It’s available only on weekdays during lunch, so plan accordingly.

Definitely recommended if you’re looking for a satisfying and authentic Chinese meal without spending too much.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Sagar Restro Bar, and overall, it turned out to be a pleasant and satisfying experience, deserving a solid four stars. The place has a welcoming vibe from the moment you enter — the lighting, seating arrangement, and overall ambience create a relaxed atmosphere that works well for both casual outings and small get-togethers. It strikes a balance between being lively and comfortable without feeling too loud or chaotic, which is something I really appreciated.

The service was quite good too. The staff was attentive, quick to take orders, and responsive throughout the visit. Even on a moderately busy day, they managed to serve everything within a reasonable time. Their politeness and readiness to help definitely added to the overall experience.

Coming to the food and drinks, Sagar Restro Bar offers a pretty decent variety. Most of the dishes we tried were flavourful and freshly prepared. The starters were particularly enjoyable — well-seasoned and cooked just right. The drinks were also nice, with good options at reasonable pricing compared to many other restro-bars. While the menu may not be extremely unique or experimental, it delivers well on the classics, and that’s more than enough for a comfortable night out.

There were, however, a few areas where the place could improve. Some dishes felt slightly inconsistent in taste, as if prepared differently on different days. Nothing too disappointing, but with a bit more consistency, the dining experience would become even better. Another small point is that while the ambience is good, certain corners of the seating area could use better lighting or layout adjustments to enhance comfort.

Despite these minor shortcomings, Sagar Restro Bar still stands out as a reliable and enjoyable place to unwind. It’s the kind of spot where you can expect good food, friendly service, and a relaxed environment without worrying about excessive noise or rushed service. I would definitely visit again and recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable restro-bar experience that’s worth the money.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gurukripa Bar on Saki Vihar Road, Powai is one of those classic neighbourhood bars that has built a strong reputation purely on the strength of its food. I recently visited with friends and overall had a very satisfying experience, making it a solid 4-star destination for anyone in and around Powai looking for good food and a lively evening.

Let me start with the food, which is undoubtedly the highlight here. We ordered several starters along with a basic main course, and every dish was well-prepared and full of flavour. The absolute star of the meal was the mutton — incredibly tender, perfectly cooked, and rich in taste. If you are a mutton lover, this place will not disappoint you. In fact, the Dehati Mutton is a must-try. It is slow-cooked beautifully, packed with traditional flavours, and has that authentic rustic taste that is hard to find these days. Easily one of the best mutton dishes you can have in this area.

The starters were fresh and satisfying, and the gravies paired very well with rotis and rice. Portion sizes are generous, making it a good value-for-money place when dining with friends or in a group.

Another thing that truly impressed me was the speed of service. Even when the bar is packed, the staff manages to serve food in a decent amount of time. This shows excellent coordination between the kitchen and the service team, which is not easy to maintain during peak hours. Despite the crowd, our orders arrived quickly and were served hot, which added to the overall positive experience.

That said, timing your visit is extremely important. I would strongly recommend avoiding Friday nights unless you enjoy a loud, high-energy crowd. The place gets extremely crowded with corporate groups, and after 7 PM, finding a table becomes next to impossible. It also gets very noisy, which personally is not my preference when I want to relax and have a peaceful conversation with friends. I prefer quieter places, and Friday nights here can feel overwhelming.

If you still plan to visit on a busy day, the best time to reach is between 6:30 PM and 7 PM. After that, the crowd increases rapidly.

The ambience is typical of a popular local bar — lively, energetic, and social. It’s not a luxury lounge, but it has its own charm for people who enjoy a bustling atmosphere.

I am also cutting one star and giving 4 stars instead of 5 because of the pan shop owner outside the bar. I strongly believe these pan shops are indirectly part of the bar experience, and it is every bar’s responsibility to ensure that the outside environment is managed well. The first impression matters, and it should reflect the quality inside.

Overall, Gurukripa Bar delivers where it matters most — excellent food, especially mutton, fast service, and good value for money. With smart timing and the right expectations, it’s a fantastic place for a satisfying evening out.

If you go, don’t miss the Dehati Mutton — it’s an absolute must-try.

featured_reviews.name: Prasad K
featured_reviews.review_text:
We tried multiple dishes at Bayroute and overall had a very pleasant experience.
The Machboos Al Kuzu was flavourful and aromatic, with beautifully spiced rice and tender lamb — a very satisfying and hearty dish.

The hummus with chicken shawarma add-on and pita bread was absolutely awesome. The hummus was creamy and rich, the shawarma was well-seasoned, and together with warm pita bread it tasted amazing.

The Kuzu (lamb dish) was cooked well and the meat was tender. It was tasty and comforting, though the flavours were on the milder side and felt a little subtle.

The baklava was a complete show, waiter crushed rose on it and  made it feel special, and it tasted amazing. Rich, flaky, and not overly sweet.

Overall, the place is slightly heavy on the pocket, but the ambience is very good, the location is convenient, and the staff is friendly and helpful, which adds a lot to the experience.
I really liked the place and would visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Mishti Khadye
featured_reviews.review_text:
For a video review check my IG page- itsmishtikhadye.

Im hoping my review along with description gives you an idea about things♥️✨

Bayroute, Powai, is a Middle Eastern dream come true! 🌅 The ambience is a warm mix of indoor & outdoor seating, with hot air balloons 🛫️ setting the perfect Middle Eastern vibe — super cozy and Instagram-worthy! 👌 Staff are friendly & attentive, and the washrooms are spotless.

Food Highlights:
- Fateh Dajaj: Succulent shredded chicken in a creamy garlic sauce with crispy bread — addictive & finger-licking good!
- Kebab Halabi: Soft, fresh bread paired with juicy kebabs — a match made in heaven.
- Lavash Crush Chicken Halabi: A biryani-like delight, mild on spice, with lavash crust (crunchy like papad) adding that wow factor.
- Dijaj Tria: A trio of chicken preparations — perfect for those wanting a taste of variety.

Desserts & Drinks:

- Greek Goddess (drink): Refreshing light berry drink — perfect for a chill vibe.

- Salted Caramel Baklava Sheikh*: My fav! Rich, nutty, and that salted caramel twist on classic baklava — divine. Remeber to share it cz it is heavy!

- Kunafa (live experience): Layers of crunchy pastry, dry fruits, and ice cream — utterly mesmerizing & drool-worthy.

Verdict: Bayroute’s food, ambience, and live kunafa prep make it a must-visit for Middle Eastern food lovers! Hot air balloons, good staff, and clean washrooms — they’ve ticked all the boxes. ⭐️

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Sonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
📍 Authentic Middle Eastern • Great Ambience • Excellent Service

From the moment we stepped in, Bayroute impressed with its warm lighting, elegant interiors, and relaxed yet refined vibe — perfect for date nights or a chill evening with friends.

✨ Food:
The menu is a celebration of Middle Eastern cuisine. The mezze platter was fresh and flavorful, with hummus and mutabbal that were beautifully balanced. The grilled kebabs were juicy and fragrant, perfectly seasoned and cooked just right. The shakshuka was rich and comforting, and the saffron rice was a great companion to every dish.

🍷 Drinks:
Pairing the food with their mocktails/cocktails elevated the experience — refreshing with the right amount of creativity.

💁‍♂️ Service:
Attentive and friendly staff who were happy to recommend dishes and explain flavours. The pacing between courses was spot-on.

💸 Value:
Pricing is on the premium side, but worth it for the quality, portions, and overall experience.

✨ Overall:
A delightful Middle Eastern escape in the heart of Powai. Food, ambience, and service all deliver — Bayroute is now a must-visit on the Mumbai dining map!
